recipes.name: Chicken Breasts with Chipotle Green Onion Gravy
ingredients_raw: salt and fresh ground pepper to taste
0.5 teaspoon chipotle chile powder, or more to taste

steps.text: Place chicken breast halves between 2 sheets of heavy plastic (resealable freezer bags work well) on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound chicken with the smooth side of a meat mallet to 1/2-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat until it begins to shimmer, about 1 minute. Reduce heat to medium; cook chicken breasts in hot oil until browned and no longer pink inside, about 5 minutes per side. Transfer cooked chicken to a warm plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.

Melt butter in the same skillet. Stir in flour and cook for about 2 minutes. Stir in chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook and stir until gravy begins to simmer and thicken, 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir in green onions and chipotle chile powder.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet and cook until heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Breasts with Chipotle Green Onion Gravy
raw_recipe.description: These simple chicken breasts are served with chipotle and green onion gravy made in the same pan with the flavorful drippings for an easy meal for two.

review.reviewBody: I was looking for something different to do with my chicken breasts and this recipe was on the front page including a video on how to prepare. So easy and tasty and a big hit with the family! Didn't have to run to the grocery store because I had everything on hand. *I lied - except for the chipotle seasoning! I did a web search and found I could use a paprika, red pepper with a dash of chili powder as a substitute. About 1/2 tsp. paprika, 1/8 red pepper and a dash of chili powder. Will look for chipotle seasoning for the next time I make this!

We were looking for something different when I came across this recipe... it was delicious! I rubbed the chicken with seasoned salt, black pepper, cayenne pepper and some "Mrs Dash" extra spicy seasoning mix. Just cooking the chicken smelled great! I used canned chipotle peppers in abodo sauce; 2 peppers and 2 tsp of sauce. It was very, very spicy! When I make it next time, I'll use the same amount of peppers and sauce but double the amount of base gravy. Everyone loved it, the only complaint was there wasn't enough sauce! I served it over egg noodles with some broccoli, smothered the whole plate in sauce.

I used chicken thighs, and as a result, there was no need for pounding the meat with a mallet (as it was already thin enough), so using thighs instead of breasts is a good option, if you are looking to eliminate that step. The flavor was excellent, the chipotle chili powder and green onions were the staples that made the whole thing come together. It did have a nice kick, but not an unreasonable amount of spice.

I've made this twice with great success. It has a place in the rotation.

My chipotle powder was old, so I used 3 teaspoons, and it was perfect. Next to the 1/2 teaspoon on the recipe, I wrote, "Ha ha ha." We like a kick. I got fresh chipotle powder today, so will probably drop it back to two teaspoons. 
I also minced four green onions instead of two tablespoons. It was definitely more than 2 TBS.
I'm going to sub this gravy for the just "meh" gravy called for with a chicken meatball recipe. 
Served with pasta and fresh steamed broccoli.

Very fast and easy dinner. I chopped up a couple of chicken thighs and browned them because that's what I had. I used no salt butter because I had chicken bouillon vs broth. Served over noodles and hubs loved it! Made a veg for the side.... Worked out great after a late workday. Will do again.

Made more gravy (more flour and more chicken stock).
Sprinkled with cheese and topped with sour cream. Served with cilantro lime rice. So quick and easy!
Chipotle powder is great. Can get spicy for those that don't care for too much spice.

I have to say I doubt I have ever followed a recipe exactly but I used it as the basis for the Chipotle Chicken I made last night for dinner. I made more than the recipe calls for since I wanted leftovers for tonite. Changes I made (I do not measure) is I used an onion instead of green onion and put them in the chicken after browning it to cook. I did cut the three large chicken breasts I had into chunks. I added extra chicken stock and added an 8 oz package of cream cheese because I wanted a creamy sauce. I kept tasting for seasoning and added more chipotle powder to taste and added garlic powder as well. I wanted it spicy but not too spicey. Served it over noodles. It was delicious and I really liked that the main seasoning was the chipotle. Usually I use it with other mexican spices so it doesn't usually stand out. It was very fast to prepare. I used cornstarch mixed with chicken stock at the end to thicken it a bit. I added some lime juice at the end to brighten it up. It was delicious and I can't wait for leftovers. I am sure chef John's original recipe is very delicious, but like I said I use recipes for ideas and my own variations.

My boyfriend and I love this recipe and have made it several times. I make the chicken stock out of bullion and add some diced onion for texture. We don't change anything else, but recommend making more of the sauce as it is super delicious over rice.

Oh, if you have an electric stove take the pan off the burner for a minute or two and let the burner cool to the recommended setting before making the sauce. I wasn't smart enough to do this the first time and just turned down the heat and started making it. The rue burned right away and I had to remake it.
Excellent! I cut/shred the chicken afterwards, double the gravy, triple the chipotle and add a carton of sour cream, and pour it all over penne.

Super fast and easy to make! Great weeknight dinner. We didn't have any chile powder on hand so we substituted a bit of sauce from a can of Chipotle Peppers in Adobo Sauce and it was delicious. It went great with broccoli and rice.
Yummy. I could not find chipotle powder so I ended up using 2 chipotle Chiles with sauce, into the gravy! It was so good. It’s a definite keeper
This was really tasty. Since my husband and I like spicy, I used 3/4 of a tsp of the ground chipotle pepper. That was perfect for us. This will be at our dinner table again.
Have made multiple times, Making it tonight... very good and easy.
I love this recipe. I add canned Chipotle peppers and the Adobe sauce.
Quick, easy and delicious. Great with rice and green beans. Would be good with mashed spuds too.
This gravy is fantastic!!! Thanks Chef John!!!
Very good, very easy and so tender! I will make this again.
